mcqs.q: The oral mucous membrane maintains its structural integrity by:
opts: Continuous renewal — desquamation of old superficial cells
mcqs.explain: The OMM continuously renews itself, shedding (desquamating) old cells at the superficial layer.

mcqs.q: The oral mucosa is continuous with the skin of the lip through the:
mcqs.explain: Anteriorly the oral mucosa is continuous with skin through the vermilion border of the lip; posteriorly it continues with pharyngeal mucosa.

mcqs.q: Masticatory mucosa (about 25%) is found on the:
opts: Gingiva and hard palate (keratinized, bound to bone)
mcqs.explain: Masticatory mucosa covers the gingiva and hard palate; it is keratinized, bound to bone and bears chewing forces.

mcqs.q: Lining mucosa (about 60%) is characteristically:
mcqs.explain: Lining mucosa (lips, cheeks, vestibule, floor of mouth, ventral tongue, soft palate, alveolar mucosa) is non-keratinized, soft, moist and distensible.

mcqs.q: Specialized (sensory) mucosa is found on the:
opts: Dorsum of the tongue (bearing taste buds)
mcqs.explain: Specialized mucosa covers the dorsum of the tongue and bears the taste buds, which have a sensory function.

mcqs.q: The functions of the oral mucosa (mnemonic PASS) are:
mcqs.explain: The OMM provides Protection, Absorption (e.g. sublingual nitrates), Sensation and Secretion (saliva).

mcqs.q: An example of absorption through the oral mucosa is:
mcqs.explain: Nitrates (e.g. glyceryl trinitrate) are absorbed sublingually through the thin floor-of-mouth mucosa.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a factor affecting the colour of the oral mucosa?
opts: Thickness and keratinization of the epithelium
mcqs.explain: Mucosal colour depends on vascularity, epithelial thickness, degree of keratinization and melanin — not tooth shape. Inflamed mucosa appears red rather than pale pink.

mcqs.q: Unlike oral mucosa, the epithelium of the skin is:
mcqs.explain: Skin epithelium is always orthokeratinized, whereas oral mucosa may be non-keratinized or (ortho- or para-) keratinized depending on region.

mcqs.q: Ectopic sebaceous glands seen in the oral cavity (upper lip, buccal/alveolar mucosa) are called:
mcqs.explain: Fordyce's spots are ectopic sebaceous glands found predominantly in the upper lip, buccal mucosa and alveolar mucosa.

mcqs.q: Compared with skin, oral mucosa lacks:
opts: Hair follicles, sweat glands and (mostly) sebaceous glands
mcqs.explain: Oral mucosa lacks hair follicles, sweat glands and (apart from Fordyce spots) sebaceous glands; it is kept moist by minor salivary glands.

mcqs.q: The three basic layers of the oral mucous membrane are:
opts: Oral epithelium, lamina propria and submucosa
mcqs.explain: The OMM consists of the oral epithelium, the lamina propria (connective tissue) and the submucosa.

mcqs.q: The oral epithelium is of the ___ type:
mcqs.explain: The oral epithelium is stratified squamous — multiple layers with flattened, scale-like superficial cells.

mcqs.q: The downward projections of epithelium into the connective tissue are called:
mcqs.explain: The epithelium–connective-tissue interface is irregular, with downward epithelial projections called rete ridges/pegs across the basement membrane.

mcqs.q: The lamina propria consists of two layers:
opts: A superficial papillary layer and a deep reticular layer
mcqs.explain: The lamina propria has a superficial papillary layer (loose, thin collagen) and a deep reticular layer (thick collagen bundles parallel to the surface).

mcqs.q: In the gingiva and hard palate, the submucosa is:
opts: Absent — the lamina propria attaches directly to periosteum (mucoperiosteum)
mcqs.explain: Gingiva and hard palate have no submucosa; the lamina propria attaches directly to the periosteum, forming a firm, inelastic 'mucoperiosteum'.

mcqs.q: The submucosa generally provides:
opts: Flexibility, containing fat, glands, large vessels and nerves
mcqs.explain: The submucosa lies between the lamina propria and bone/muscle, containing loose fat and glandular tissue with large vessels and nerves — providing flexibility.

mcqs.q: Why is the firmness of the oral mucosa clinically important?
opts: Loose mucosa (lips/cheek) vs firm mucosa (gingiva/palate) affects injections
mcqs.explain: Buccal mucosa and lips are loose and pliable, whereas gingiva and hard palate are firm — important when administering injections.

mcqs.q: Keratinized oral mucosa includes the gingiva, hard palate and the:
mcqs.explain: Keratinized mucosa is found on the gingiva, hard palate and vermilion border of the lip (and may be ortho- or parakeratinized).

mcqs.q: The connective tissue of the oral mucosa is the lamina propria; in the skin it is the:
mcqs.explain: The connective tissue of oral mucosa is the lamina propria; in skin the equivalent connective tissue layer is the dermis (skin = epidermis + dermis).

mcqs.q: The interface between the oral epithelium and connective tissue is a structureless layer called the:
mcqs.explain: The epithelium and connective tissue meet at a structureless layer called the basement membrane, with rete pegs giving an irregular interface.

mcqs.q: Lining mucosa covers all of the following EXCEPT the:
mcqs.explain: The hard palate is masticatory mucosa; lining mucosa covers the floor of mouth, ventral tongue, alveolar mucosa, cheeks, lips and soft palate.

saqs.q: Classify the oral mucosa by function (with percentages).
saqs.a: Masticatory (25%) — gingiva, hard palate (keratinized); Lining (60%) — lips, cheeks, floor, etc. (non-keratinized); Specialized (15%) — tongue dorsum (taste buds).

saqs.q: List the four functions of the oral mucosa (PASS).
Name the three layers of the oral mucous membrane.
Describe the two layers of the lamina propria.
saqs.a: Superficial papillary layer (loose, thin, irregular collagen) and deep reticular layer (thick collagen bundles parallel to surface).

saqs.q: What is mucoperiosteum and where is it found?
saqs.a: Where there is no submucosa, the lamina propria attaches directly to periosteum — a firm, inelastic attachment found in the gingiva and hard palate.

saqs.q: Give three differences between skin and oral mucosa.
saqs.a: Skin is always orthokeratinized, has hair/sweat/sebaceous glands, and is dry; oral mucosa may be non-/ortho-/parakeratinized, is moist (minor salivary glands), smoother and lacks those adnexa (except Fordyce spots).
Downward projections of epithelium into the connective tissue (across the basement membrane), giving an irregular interface.
